input.quote: 13.1 IBM assumes and will assume ownership and MSL assigns and will assign all intellectual and industrial property rights for hardware, software, design and documentation of all Products delivered under this Agreement
input.rationale: The IP bargain sits at or above our preferred position and is directionally in our favour. § 13.1 (p0197) vests ownership of all IP in the hardware, software, design and documentation of Products in IBM, with an express present and future assignment by MSL; p0198 extends IBM ownership and MSL assignment to inventions made on Products and on IBM processes and systems, MSL's carve-out being only a right to use such inventions "in the performance of its obligations hereunder" — i.e. service delivery, not independent exploitation. Ownership by assignment is stronger than the fallback's perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense, so those licence elements are subsumed. § 20.0 (p1088) leaves commonly used production tooling with MSL, which matches the fallback allowance for Vendor generic tools. There is no joint-ownership language anywhere in the Agreement, and no assignment of IBM IP or IBM data to MSL: § 13.3 a) (p0208) confirms MSL receives no rights in IBM's pre-existing IP save a royalty-free licence to use disclosed confidential information "necessary to manufacture Products solely for IBM" — a use limited to providing the contracted services. Two preferred sub-points are less than fully articulated and are noted rather than redlined: there is no express statement that MSL retains its own pre-existing IP (an omission that operates in our favour), and no standing perpetual/irrevocable/royalty-free licence back of MSL IP embedded in Products, with § 24.1 (p1136) stating that "MSL conveys to IBM no software title or license under the intellectual property rights of MSL" — that clause governs transition-period system access software rather than Product deliverables, whose IP § 13.1 assigns to us in full. No redline is warranted.
